description: This case study is an overview paper by Dennis Lottis of HafenCity University Hamburg and Fraunhofer IEE Kassel on a digital twin for the District LAB test facility, published in the HCU Technical Infrastructure Management Insights series. The abstract explains that transformation of district heating grids to renewable and waste heat supply faces economic obstacles and that digitalisation looks promising; the thesis will create a simulation model containing the essential thermo-hydraulic components and control structures of the test facility, turn it into a digital twin with access to its hardware, and develop and test a predictive optimisation of the operating strategy. The text sets out the planned methods and work steps and shows first results of theoretical investigations. Access: free PDF through the German National Library link; no licence is stated. Coverage is one experimental district heating facility in Germany. Caveats: this is a work-in-progress overview, only the abstract and introduction were read here, and no data or model release was found. It suits capacity planning and resilience studies of heat network operation and digital twin methods, and it relates to the dynamic district heating network model catalogued here as model-dynamic-district-heating-network-model-discrete-event-simulation-aalto.

name: A digital twin for the District LAB test facility: simulation model and predictive operation of a district heating test bed (HafenCity University and Fraunhofer IEE)
outcomes: The paper presents planned methods and first theoretical results for a doctoral thesis: build a simulation model of the District LAB experimental facility containing its thermo-hydraulic components and control structures, transfer it into a digital twin with access to the hardware, and develop and test a predictive optimisation of the operating strategy. It argues that district heating decarbonisation in Germany needs nationwide expansion and transformation of grids, and that digitalisation such as model-based planning and machine learning can counter cost obstacles.
